_about: Definitions layer for experiment 1. Written before translation, from the target record only (README.md excluded from every source pass). Each entry cites the record document that defines it as path:line into the target repo at commit 48e66ce04a4d9f06771c42f89cb37b075583c5f6; full quotes are in sources/*.md. Where the record conflicts with itself both sides are listed under 'conflicts' and NOT resolved. Translators receive this file and the brief; they never receive the sources or the inventory.

tiers._note: Closed enum for the ledger's tier field. Free text about the instrument goes in venue.
tiers.raw: mechanical match with no judgment; in arc 2, 'raw' = strict panel-majority truth or a single-wave seat verdict with no re-adjudication (BP/ROUND4_DEV_TABLE.json:2; BP/ITERATION_NOTES.md:272-275)
tiers.panel: a frontier-judge panel ruling: arc 1 = the 3-judge frontier panel per behaviour (data/behaviours.json provenance); arc 2 = 3-instance panels, majority supersedes (BP/ROUND4_PREREG.md:24-25)
tiers.adjudicated: a seat ruling folded with panel/human rulings; in arc 2 includes match-or-defensible and match-or-adjudicated-defensible ('headline') views (BP/ROUND4_PREREG.md:106-113)
tiers.human: an owner ruling (entries headed 'MATT RULING', decision.json signed_by)
tiers.live_run: produced by running a committed script now; record the command and wall clock
tiers.filesystem: existence or shape of a committed file
tiers.stated: a number stated in a document with no re-derivation artifact
tiers.cove: independently re-derived by a second party from data on disk; the record's own 'CoVe' (BP/L1L2_REVIEW_DISPOSITION.md:12-13; BP/ITERATION_NOTES.md:836-838)

entries.definition: fraction of seat-engaged nodes ruled relevant by the truth tier
entries.authoritative: per venue: round-4 dev behaviours = BP/ROUND4_DEV_TABLE.json (raw and headline columns, 'Both publish'); tradeoffs repair loop = the per-attempt BP/ITER*_SCORED.json with BP/ITER2_REMEASURE_SCORED.json declared FINAL for attempts 2-3
entries.denominator: varies and is not reconciled by the record: a 40-node stratified engaged draw (round 4); 20-node draws (repair loop, n='20+20'); a CLOSED population (harm, n=17); the exhaustive ruled engaged set (user-autonomy, 32/122). Always record which.
conflicts: sample view (n=20 draws carry ±~0.2, BP/ITERATION_NOTES.md:257-258) vs exhaustive view (BP/ITERATION_NOTES.md:529-531)
hazards: the same numeric value can appear at two attempts or two tiers (e.g. a raw and a panel figure for the same attempt in one line, BP/ITERATION_NOTES.md:272-275); carry attempt AND tier on every value
an attempt's figure may carry an adjusted companion in the same entry (quarantine-adjusted, BP/ITER3_ATTEMPT4_SCORED.json:190); record both as separate claims linked by supersession

entries.definition: share of tool declines the truth tier rules NOT relevant
entries.denominator: CONFLICT: panel-cited nodes only (PREREG_panel_equivalence) vs a uniform 40-node not-engaged draw (round 4). Record which population.
conflicts: attempt-2 decline recorded as 0.6 (BP/ITER1_ATTEMPT2_SCORED.json:7; BP/ITERATION_NOTES.md:154) and as 0.55 (BP/ITER2_REMEASURE_SCORED.json:29)

entries.term: recall against truth / declined nodes panel-relevant
entries.definition: fraction of truth-relevant nodes the seat engaged; its complement is reported as 'declined nodes that are panel-relevant' (not-engaged false negatives)
entries.authoritative: BP/ITER2_REMEASURE_SCORED.json panel_tier_misses.not_engaged_FN per attempt; pooled figures in the ledger entry that states them
entries.denominator: pooled declined nodes over the frozen draws it pools; a pooled value carries snapshot=pooled plus the attempt set
hazards: numerator collision: the same numerator can appear on adjacent lines with different denominators and different metrics (a precision and a recall-side figure); carry the metric name and the denominator population, never just the fraction

entries.term: raw / panel tier / single-wave / uniform panel tier / re-measurement
entries.definition: raw = strict panel-majority truth or a single seat's (single-wave) verdict; panel tier = 3-instance panel majority; uniform panel tier = every node in the frozen draws re-adjudicated at panel tier; re-measurement = re-adjudicating the SAME frozen samples at a higher tier, never a new draw
hazards: single-wave self-agreement is 0.846 (BP/CALCULUS_RUNBOOK.md:130-132): a single-wave figure is not a panel figure even for the same draw

entries.definition: a view in which a node carrying opposing unanimous panel rulings on identical text under the identical brief is scored as non-error ('defensible by contradiction'), or in which a miss adjudicated defensible by a one-pass blind seat is scored as non-error; 'headline' is the round-4 name for match-or-adjudicated-defensible, always published beside raw
entries.authoritative: BP/ROUND4_DEV_TABLE.json headline column (dev behaviours); BP/ITER2_REMEASURE_SCORED.json addendum_matt_ruling_defensibility (tradeoffs)
hazards: the defensibility pass 'cannot move a cell below its raw value, only up'; a headline figure is never lower than its raw
a registered match-or-defensible certification pass and a defensibility overlay scored alongside raw are different events; record which registration (by file name, band, or amendment id) a run cites

entries.definition: per-behaviour match-or-adjudicated-defensible rates measured on the assembled truth ledger the loop iterated against, before round-4 certification; explicitly 'NOT yet certified'
entries.authoritative: BP/HANDOFF_CURRENT.md (the line that states it); certification cells in BP/ROUND4_DEV_TABLE.json are the out-of-sample counterpart
conflicts: all-truth is called composition-biased and 'never' to be scored on (BP/L1L2_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW.md:314-316; BP/L1L2_REVIEW_DISPOSITION.md:66-68) while HANDOFF_CURRENT.md:33-39 uses it as the baseline
hazards: provenance region: this figure lives below the starred block of the handoff; record provenance_region
the same line carries a struck value ('human-panelist baseline 71%', flagged NO source artifact at BP/HANDOFF_CURRENT.md:210-211); translate it with supersession=struck

entries.term: certification / round 4 / falsifiers F1-F5 / band / floor
entries.definition: round 4 certifies the three dev behaviours on nodes never before ruled, converting in-sample criterion standing into an out-of-sample claim, scored ONCE; falsifiers F1 (engaged precision below band floor), F2 (decline below floor), F3 (≥3 unanimous-relevant not-engaged nodes sharing a new locus), F4 (>30% panels split), F5 (single-vs-panel overturn >10% → escalate); bands are in NODES (±2 per cell)
entries.authoritative: BP/ROUND4_DEV_TABLE.json (raw_verdict, headline_verdict per behaviour); per-behaviour BP/round4_*_scored*.json
conflicts: two registered band sets: all-truth-derived (BP/ROUND4_PREREG.md:70-74, kept as a recorded erratum) vs lineage-derived superseding bands (BP/ROUND4_PREREG.md:214-220)

helpfulness has three scored files with three different raw cells: round4_helpfulness_scored.json 0.625/0.625 (VOIDED canary attempt 1, E1), _v2 0.575/0.85 (re-run), _final_raw 0.625/0.875 (after F5 escalation; the one the dev table uses). Only the first is marked void in the record.
hazards: file naming asymmetry: caution and harm are round4_<slug>_scored_raw.json; helpfulness is round4_helpfulness_scored_final_raw.json; no file round4_help*_scored_raw.json exists and the record does not say why
'certification ran to completion' and 'certification passed' are different facts: record the raw_verdict text (e.g. 'F1 FIRES', 'IN BAND') with every certification claim
repair-loop predictions use P1-P4, not F1-F5

entries.term: attempt / iteration / block / draw / frozen draw / pooled / seed / seal
entries.definition: attempt 1 = the transfer measurement (frozen, never re-measured); attempts 2+ = repair measurements; iteration = the runbook cycle producing an attempt (iter 1 → attempt 2, iter 2 → attempt 3, iter 3 → attempt 4); block = a working block, the record's session-like unit, marked autonomous/unattended only when it was (unmarked = attended); draw = a seeded sample of nodes; frozen draw = a draw re-used for re-measurement; pooled = a figure over more than one draw; seed = the registered RNG base; seal = a seeded 25% of exhaustive purchases held out single-use
hazards: attempt 1 and attempt 3 can share a numeric value at different tiers; never match on value alone

pooling is used for the pooled panel-tier figure (BP/ITERATION_NOTES.md:274-275) and prohibited across seats (BP/L1L2_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW.md:108); record pooled figures with the set pooled and do not merge them with per-attempt figures

entries.definition: dev behaviours = helpfulness, harm-avoidance-to-third-parties, avoiding-over-and-under-caution (the three round-4 certifies); repair-loop behaviours = how-to-approach-tradeoffs (iterations 1-3, attempts 1-4) and user-autonomy (attempt-1 provisional, exhaustive 0.262); never-consulted block-2 behaviours also named: proportionate-risk, general-welfare, harmlessness-to-user, objectivity-on-contested-questions
hazards: a source may say 'tuned', 'mature', 'dev', 'iterated' for different sets; translate the behaviour NAME the span gives, never a class word

entries.term: panel / judges / panel-v5 / majority / split / dispute / quarantine
entries.definition: frontier panel = data/behaviours.json, judges sol / kimi / fable / opus / kimi-k2 (3 per behaviour, 5 distinct); panel-v5 = data/panel-v5/, externally authored, 9 behaviours × 589 passages, comparison layer only, never truth; majority supersedes single rulings; 2-1 majorities are 'split'; a dispute is a disagreement between seat and panel or between panels; quarantine = removing dispute resolutions from the instrument after a tripwire fires
conflicts: panel-v5 positive rates: reviewer 0.012/0.044/0.007 (BP/L1L2_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW.md:297) vs driver re-derivation 0.085/0.098/0.071 (BP/L1L2_REVIEW_DISPOSITION.md:35-37)
three relevance ledgers with three constructs all called 'relevance' (BP/L1L2_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW.md:296-300)
hazards: opposing unanimous panels on the same node exist (l3239_3382_n005, BP/ITERATION_NOTES.md:284-289); when a span records two rulings on one node, translate BOTH as separate claims marked contested; never let recency or dict order pick

entries.definition: panel-internal agreement = inter-judge agreement on relevance verdicts over the same set, proposed as the ceiling and recorded as CURRENTLY UNMEASURED; test-retest = a seat's self-agreement (Fable single-wave 0.846); human-panelist baseline 71% = a figure asserted in the handoff and flagged as having NO source artifact
hazards: do not translate seat self-agreement, mint stability (0.98), split rates, or the owner's 21/22 spot-check as 'panel-internal agreement'; each is its own metric name

entries.definition: node = a unit of the arc-2 document graph (773 in root_graph.production.json; 183 translated per coverage_translated.json); passage = the panel's unit (589 in the true Model Spec universe); span = a line range attached to a node, optionally carrying a quote (846 spans, 602 with quotes); definition = (a) the behaviour definition text a seat receives, (b) one of the 100 query-class corpus items, (c) a norm-free 'definitional lane' node
hazards: coverage figures exist over nodes (39/39) and over definitions (94/100, 100 defs); record the unit with every coverage figure
passages→nodes is not an identity map (BP/L1L2_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW.md:312)

entries.term: erratum / recurrence / CoVe / tripwire / seat / certificate / brief-local / venue / handoff / seed
entries.definition: erratum = an appended correction (registered numbers are never edited); numbered errata run #13-#21 in the ledger, four are unnumbered (entries 0001, 0004, 0009, 0013) and the ledger's own series tally counts them; recurrence = the record's own 'Nth instance/recurrence' of a defect class; CoVe = driver re-derivation of a reviewer's claim from data on disk (never expanded in the record); tripwire = a registered disagreement threshold whose firing is mechanical (quarantine or re-run); seat = a dispatched model instance receiving only a packet; certificate = a measured parity result licensing a cheaper tier, brief-local and task-class-local; venue = the concrete instrument configuration (wave+panel, all-Fable, certified-Opus, recovered lineage); handoff = a fresh session booting from committed files ('no compaction ritual, no handoff prompt'); seed = RNG base
hazards: 'seat' in the ledger = a dispatched model instance; 'seats' in SFE/machine/query.py = a governance role with a producer and validator. Same word, two ontologies.
'reset' = a provider usage-window (capacity) reset, never a context reset (BP/HANDOFF_CURRENT.md:186-188; BP/ITERATION_NOTES.md:541-545)
'block' = a working block; unmarked blocks are attended

entries.definition: Matthews correlation coefficient, THE PRIMARY METRIC of benchmark.py; 0 by construction for degenerate predictors
entries.authoritative: SFE/benchmark.py output on the named annotation config; HANDOFF tables are stated copies

entries.variants: at least 30 distinct tool MCC values exist, separated by threshold_rule (in_sample @0.18, label_free, Otsu, LOBO, oracle, dev, best-compliant, ablations) and by universe (published vs true); see sources/arc1_extraction.md §1 table
conflicts: whether MCC is the metric at all: 'NOT MCC' (SFE/HANDOFF.md:61) vs 'Use MCC as the primary metric' (SFE/HANDOFF.md:592)

the in-sample figure is described by the record itself as 'a CEILING, not a result' (hindsight threshold)

the small-model v2 panel (gpt-mini/haiku/qwen-small) is 'NEVER THE BAR'; label any judge figure by roster

entries.term: measurement modes: in-sample / fresh-draw / held-out (sealed) / generalization (transfer) / cross-document
entries.definition: five non-interchangeable modes: (1) in-sample = on the accumulated adjudicated ledger ('all-truth'); (2) fresh-draw = new nodes with every prior-ruled node excluded, same behaviours; (3) held-out/sealed = a seeded partition of already-bought truth, withheld and single-use; (4) generalization/transfer = new behaviours never consulted (attempt 1 is the transfer verdict; attempts 2+ measure the repair, never transfer); (5) cross-document = a second document, which does not exist in the record and is stated as not measurable
conflicts: round-4 registered bands were derived from all-truth (BP/ROUND4_PREREG.md:69-74) against contract §9e which forbids it; erratum E4 re-registers lineage bands so the file holds two registered prediction sets, the first retained as 'a recorded erratum'

hazards: the record states thirteen explicit 'never report one as the other' rules (sources/hazards_extraction.md §3.4); every value carries its mode, attempt index, pool, and band basis
no glossary in the record defines 'in-sample' or 'fresh draw'; both are defined only by what a pool excludes
'F1' names both an adversarial-review finding and a falsifier (BP/GENERALIZATION_BUILD_SPEC.md:53-61); record which

entries.term: opposing panel rulings on one node / defensible by contradiction
entries.definition: a node can carry two unanimous panels on identical text under the identical brief with opposite verdicts (worked example: l3239_3382_n005); the scorer's recency precedence rules by default and the record flags this as unsafe; the owner's ruling scores such nodes as non-error in the match-or-defensible view only when both panels are full and unanimous; a 2-1 panel vs a wave does not qualify and stays contested-pending
hazards: translate each ruling on such a node as its own claim, mark the pair contested, never pick one

entries.definition: the stage-4 go/no-go audit of translation fidelity (module vs span), blind Fable auditors per cohort, rule: ≥85% faithful in the new-prompt cohort or pause; 16 cohorts; scope is ASP fidelity, explicitly partitioned from relevance matching
hazards: two earliest cohorts lack 'total' and 'verdict' fields; a per-cohort rate needs both

conventions.ledger_entry_format: '## NNNN — TITLE, YYYY-MM-DD'; entry 0000 embeds its date in the title; the three redacted stubs carry the date in parentheses. No entry carries a time. Entries 0000-0031 are all dated 2026-08-24 (32 entries); 0032-0043 are dated 2026-08-25. Sort by entry number, never by date. (sources/hazards_extraction.md §7)
conventions.ordering: entry numbers are strictly monotone with the introducing commit's date for all 44 entries (checked); the order relation for ledger events is (date, entry number); for commits, (commit date, first-parent ordinal). Introducing commit of an entry: git log -S '## NNNN — ' --reverse (prefix only: six headings were rewritten on 2026-08-31, so searching the full current title finds the wrong commit).
conventions.append_only: 45 commits touch ITERATION_NOTES.md; 44 are pure appends; exactly one deletes lines: 6d01415b (2026-08-31, +89/−121, 'Publication prep ... redact operational plumbing'). It replaced three entries by stubs marked '— [operational; redacted]' (0002, 0008, 0021), stripped quantitative operational data (usage %, points, token counts) from retained entries, replaced named owner attributions and verbatim quoted speech with role language ('Matt: ...' → 'RULING:' / 'the project owner'), and renamed the headings of 0032-0034. 29 retained entries were edited without a marker. (sources/hazards_extraction.md §6c, §8)
conventions.redaction_marker: the only in-place marker form is '— [operational; redacted]', three instances, all in ITERATION_NOTES.md. The commit says it redacted 'across ~60 docs' and modified 53 .md files; only the ledger received markers. Examples of unmarked edits with deletions: HANDOFF_CURRENT.md (removed a pre-existing ⚠️ correction line), ROUND4_PREREG.md, EXPERIMENTS.md, GENERALIZATION_PREREG_DRAFT.md. Pre-redaction content: git show 6d01415b^:<path>.
conventions.prereg_integrity: all eight prereg documents plus PREREG_panel_equivalence.md were edited by 6d01415b. PREREG_panel_equivalence.md's own text says 'Editing this file after approval voids the registration' and carries a sha sidecar (PREREG_panel_equivalence.sha256) that matched immediately before 6d01415b and does not match after. The record nowhere adjudicates this; translators record the mechanical facts (file, hunk, sha before/after) and nothing more.
conventions.marking_systems: three coexisting systems that do not agree: (a) ledger: append-only, superseded entries are withdrawn by a later numbered entry (0042 withdraws 0041); (b) handoffs: star count = recency of a state block, ⛔ = do not act on, ⚠️ = caveat, ~~strike~~ = retracted-but-retained; (c) delete-don't-annotate: 'A superseded number left in a doc is an instruction, not a footnote. Delete it' (SFE/HANDOFF.md:1357), applied in some sections and contradicted by 'nothing was silently deleted' (SFE/HANDOFF.md:292-294). (sources/hazards_extraction.md §1)
conventions.git_totals: 656 commits, 2026-08-02 to 2026-09-01; one merge; HEAD (branch d3-worked-example) == origin/main == public/main == 48e66ce0; local main is behind. Run git log from the pinned hash, never from 'main'.
conventions.git_trailers: 620/656 commits carry one co-author trailer: 'Claude Fable 5' 460, 'Claude Opus 5 (1M context)' 104, 'Claude Opus 5' 14, 'Qwen-Coder' 41 (lowercase 'Co-authored-by'), 'Qwen Code' 1; 36 carry none. 'Claude-Session:' trailers on 361 commits. The driver's model tier is recoverable only from these trailers, never from the span. Two Opus trailer strings are one tier; a case-sensitive grep misses the Qwen commits.
conventions.history_rewrites: reflog complete (661 entries); no rebase, filter-branch, or force-push recorded; six 'reset' entries are no-ops; exactly one amend (HEAD@{416}, message-only, diff empty, orphan 16bbbe59 survives). Consistent with 'History is published unrewritten' except for that message-only amend.
conventions.withdrawal_commit_conventions: no fixed prefix; keywords in subjects: 'withdrawn:' (bf0d4978, 365d68b3, ecb2e9df, 86a703c1), 'WITHDRAW' (47779d8c), 'retracted' (94c24b3d, 2254f925, c04b80ef), 'rescinded' (a7a8ca8c), 'struck' (ae00660f, 12181ba0, 999f1403), 'Erratum #N' (#13-#21 each has a subject-visible commit), 'VOIDED' (2b1505bb). Subject-only and full-message keyword filters return different sets; record which filter produced a list.
conventions.overloaded_words: reset = provider capacity reset; block = working block (attended unless marked autonomous); seat = model instance (ledger) vs governance role (machine/query.py); seed = RNG base; venue = instrument configuration; withheld = blinding a seat, not publication redaction; '[REDACTED]' inside specs/openai-model-spec/model_spec.md is upstream source content, not this project's redaction; F1 = falsifier or review finding; 'definition' has three senses (see node/passage/span/definition entry).
